name: JLL (Jones Lang LaSalle)

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (JLL logo.svg, hosted on Commons)

description: JLL is one of the world's largest commercial real estate service firms. It does not own the buildings; clients (corporate tenants, landlords, investors, governments) pay it fees. About 77 percent of its $26.1 billion of 2025 revenue is Real Estate Management Services, mostly running facilities and managing projects and properties for big occupiers under three-to-seven-year contracts, much of its revenue being client-dedicated staff and vendor costs that clients reimburse. The profit is in the transaction lines: Leasing Advisory (commissions on leases signed) and Capital Markets (commissions on property sales and debt placement) made 65 percent of 2025 segment Adjusted EBITDA on 21 percent of revenue. A small asset manager, LaSalle Investment Management ($86.4 billion under management), earns advisory and incentive fees. Earnings swing with deal volume and have a seasonal peak in the fourth quarter.

sub.name: Property brokers, managers, data and listings

hq.note: 200 East Randolph Drive, Chicago (8-K cover page filed 2026-09-30)

employees.note: 58.6 thousand professional non-reimbursable plus 54.6 thousand directly reimbursable employees (costs of the latter are repaid by clients, mainly in Real Estate Management Services); about two-thirds are outside the US (FY2025 10-K, Human Capital)

businessLines.name: Real Estate Management Services
businessLines.how: Corporate occupiers and landlords pay recurring fees (fixed fee, cost-plus, guaranteed maximum or percent of collections) to run their facilities, projects and properties, plus reimbursement of the staff and vendor costs JLL passes through. Revenue is large and steady but the margin on it is small; incentive fees are earned for hitting cost or satisfaction targets.
businessLines.description: Workplace Management (outsourced facility management for corporates, about 2.8 billion sq ft managed), Project Management (design, fit-out and construction management; Tetris brand in Europe), Property Management (about 2.9 billion sq ft for owners) and Portfolio Services and Other.

businessLines.name: Leasing Advisory
businessLines.how: A commission paid once when a lease is signed, usually a percentage of the lease's total rent commitment (or a fee per square foot), by the landlord (agency) or the tenant (representation). Revenue tracks leasing activity and is seasonal toward year end.
businessLines.description: Agency leasing (for landlords; about 19,500 transactions, 340 million sq ft in 2025), tenant representation (about 23,500 transactions, 569 million sq ft) and advisory/consulting.

businessLines.name: Capital Markets Services
businessLines.how: Brokerage and placement fees as a percentage of the value of a property sale or financing, paid when the deal closes; valuation fees per assignment; and an annual servicing fee on each loan it services (a share of collections), which is the steady part.
businessLines.description: Investment sales brokerage, debt and equity advisory, valuation and risk advisory, and multifamily loan origination and servicing (Fannie Mae DUS lender; servicing portfolio about $140.3 billion). About $258 billion of client transactions in 2025.

businessLines.name: Investment Management (LaSalle Investment Management)
businessLines.how: Annual advisory fees on capital committed or the marked value of assets managed, occasional transaction fees on buying and selling, and incentive fees when funds beat return hurdles (lumpy). JLL also co-invests its own capital, which creates equity gains or losses.
businessLines.description: Real estate fund and separate-account manager for institutions and individuals; assets under management $86.4 billion at 2025-12-31 (about 34 percent in open-end funds), $505.8 million of JLL co-investments.

businessLines.name: Software and Technology Solutions
businessLines.how: Subscription fees for cloud software recognised over the contract term, plus professional services fees for implementation. Still loss-making at the segment level.
businessLines.description: Property software sold by subscription (Building Engines, Corrigo) plus implementation and managed services.

brands.name: JLL
brands.share: Principal trading name; the four non-investment segments are $25.7B of $26.1B revenue

brands.name: Tetris
brands.segment: Project Management (fit-out, refurbishment and design, mainly Europe)

brands.name: JLL Spark Global Ventures funds
brands.share: $340.1M fair value of proptech investments at 2025-12-31
